exec: pm.test('Every card has likesCount, isLiked and status', () => list.forEach(v => { pm.expect(v.likesCount).to.be.a('number'); pm.expect(v.isLiked).to.be.a('boolean'); pm.expect(['ended', 'active', 'upcoming']).to.include(v.status); }));
// the first vacation Dana did NOT like — the like tests below use it
for (let i = 1; i < list.length; i++) pm.expect(new Date(list[i].startDate) >= new Date(list[i - 1].startDate)).to.be.true;
pm.test('The rest of the vacations', () => pm.expect(page.vacations.length).to.eql(Math.min(9, page.total - 9)));
pm.test('Their start date is after today', () => list.forEach(v => pm.expect(new Date(v.startDate) > new Date()).to.be.true));
pm.test('Only vacations I liked', () => pm.response.json().vacations.forEach(v => pm.expect(v.isLiked).to.be.true));

request.description: Calls Gemini (structured JSON). Takes a few seconds.
Gemini picks a tool of the MCP server, the MCP client calls it, Gemini writes the answer.
The MCP server over HTTP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0). Any MCP client can connect with the same Bearer token.
